title: Every save overwrites the whole notes list from one tab's memory; a second tab silently destroys the first tab's notes
evidence: saveNotes serialises the module-level `notes` array of the calling tab and replaces the single 'notes' key. grep of app.js and store.js finds no 'storage' event listener and no re-read of localStorage before a write (app.js:17-18 loads once at start; app.js:33 commit() writes the in-memory array).
failing_case: Open the app in tab A and tab B (both load N notes). In tab A press New note and type 'Rent due' (saved to storage). In tab B edit any old note. Tab B's debounce fires, saveNotes writes B's array, which does not contain 'Rent due'. The note is gone from storage; tab B and any reload never show it. Tab A still shows 'Saved' because its own write succeeded.
remediation: Listen for the window 'storage' event and merge or reload on change, or re-read the stored list and merge by id (latest `updated` wins) inside saveNotes before writing. Store notes per key or use a version counter so a stale writer is detected and refused.

title: 'Search notes' matches titles only, so text in a note's body is never found
evidence: renderList filters on n.title alone; n.body is not consulted anywhere in app.js. The control is labelled 'Search notes' (index.html:14) with no hint that it is a title filter. New notes start as 'Untitled' (store.js:14), so most notes are findable only by that word until renamed.
failing_case: Create a note, leave the title 'Untitled', type 'dentist at 3pm' in the body. Type 'dentist' in Search notes. The list shows 'No notes match "dentist".' although the note exists, and the user concludes it was lost.
remediation: Match against title and body (`(n.title + ' ' + n.body).toLowerCase().includes(q)`), or relabel the field 'Filter by title' and say so in the empty message.

requirement.why: The label says 'Search notes' and notes have a body; no document states the search scope.

title: Every list render destroys the focused button, so keyboard and screen-reader focus drops to the page top after selecting or deleting a note
evidence: The click handler (app.js:161-166) calls selectNote or deleteNote, both of which end in renderList, which replaces every <li> and <button> with new nodes. Nothing restores focus (focus() is called only at app.js:109 for a new note). The pagehide and blur paths are not involved.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs to a note button and presses Enter. selectNote runs, the button node is removed, document.activeElement becomes <body>. The next Tab starts at the top of the page again, and the screen reader announces nothing about the opened note. The same happens after confirming Delete: focus is lost from the removed row. Opening several notes in a row needs a full re-tab from the top each time (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order, level A).
remediation: After renderList, restore focus: remember the active element's data-id and `.open` or `.del` class before replacing, and re-focus the matching new button (or the next row, or #new after the last delete). Better, update rows in place by id instead of replacing the whole list.

quote: try { localStorage.setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw); } catch (e) { /* storage is already failing; the load message says so */ }
title: Backup failure is swallowed, yet the load message still says the unreadable data 'was kept'; the next save then overwrites it
evidence: backupRaw returns nothing and loadNotes ignores the outcome: store.js:47-48, 52-53 and 65-67 always return a problem sentence claiming the data 'was kept under notes-backup'. The comment says the message reports the failure, but the message text at those lines is unconditional. After the failed load, notes is [] and the first New note calls saveNotes (app.js:33), which replaces STORAGE_KEY, the only remaining copy.
failing_case: localStorage holds a large unreadable 'notes' value (for example 3 MB of truncated JSON) in a 5 MB quota. On load JSON.parse throws, setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw) throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed, and the user is told the data was kept under 'notes-backup'. The user presses New note; the small valid list replaces the original value. The recoverable data is gone and the message was false.
remediation: Make backupRaw return whether the write succeeded, and have loadNotes word the problem as 'could not be backed up and will be overwritten' when it did not. Also refuse to overwrite STORAGE_KEY with a fresh list until a backup exists or the user confirms.

title: Search, title and body field borders are about 1.4:1 against the page, under the 3:1 needed to see the controls
evidence: --line is #d5d8dc (styles.css:6) on a #ffffff field inside a #f7f7f5 page; computed contrast about 1.43:1 against white and lower against the page. The only other cue is the 0.875rem grey label. The disabled state (styles.css:25) paints the fields #f7f7f5, identical to the page background, so with the border at 1.3:1 the empty-state editor is almost invisible.
failing_case: A low-vision user at first run, with no notes, sees two disabled boxes that blend into the page; the text fields' edges are not distinguishable in sunlight or on a dim screen. WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA) requires 3:1 for the boundary that identifies an input.
remediation: Use a border colour of at least 3:1 against both the field and the page (for example #767a80 at 4.5:1 on white), and give the disabled state a visible dashed or tinted outline.

title: The load-time warning about unreadable or skipped notes is replaced by 'Saved' at the first action
evidence: app.js:179 shows loaded.problem in the same status element that commit() writes. The first New note, edit or delete calls commit, which sets the text to 'Saved' and removes the error class. The message is the only place that names the notes-backup key.
failing_case: Stored data is corrupt. On load the user sees 'Saved notes could not be read. The unreadable data was kept under "notes-backup".' They press New note; the status becomes 'Saved' and the instruction on where the old data is can no longer be found.
remediation: Show load problems in their own persistent element (dismissible) rather than the transient save status.

title: New note created while a search is active is selected but hidden from the list
evidence: createNote does not clear els.search. renderList (app.js:61-63) filters by the current query, and the new note's title 'Untitled' (store.js:14) does not match most queries. After selectNote, the editor shows the note but the list shows 'No notes match ...'.
failing_case: Type 'rent' in Search notes, press New note. The editor opens an 'Untitled' note, the list reads 'No notes match "rent".', and the note the user is typing in is not in the list or selectable again after switching away.
remediation: Clear the search box (and the shared results) in createNote before rendering.
